currency.mpRateNote: Monetary Policy Rate cut 250bps to 10.75% at the 30 September 2026 MPC (from 13.25%), the lowest in several years, as inflation eased back inside the BoZ target band. Prior path: 13.25% held at the August 2026 MPC (26 Aug); 25bps cut from 13.50% at the May 2026 MPC; 75bps cut from 14.25% on 11 Feb 2026. The 30 Sep decision coincided with the 10% copper-concentrate export duty taking effect and the start of IMF successor-programme talks.

trendAnalysis.outlook: The kwacha gave back a little of late-September/early-October firmness in the latest session, with the USD/ZMW market mid at ~K19.7508 (open.er-api.com, 9 Oct) versus ~K19.7425 in the prior snapshot - a marginal +0.04% move. The softening was broad but small: GBP (26.1076, +0.04%), EUR (22.136, +0.03%), ZAR (1.1887, +0.24%) and CNY (2.9412, +0.03%) all cost slightly more kwacha, while BWP (1.4093, +2.01%) moved most. The pair remains within the broad 18.40-19.80 consolidation band. The policy backdrop remains the 30 September 2026 MPC, at which the BoZ cut the MPR 250bps to 10.75% - the lowest in several years - as inflation (6.1% y/y in September, per ZamStats) returned inside the 6-8% target band; that trims the carry support that buoyed the kwacha earlier in 2026. Import demand, copper-price swings, the pace of further BoZ easing and the 9 October opening of the 14th National Assembly (2026/2027 policy direction) are the near-term reference points.
trendAnalysis.projection3m: USD/ZMW 18.50–19.80 range. Post-election policy continuity and IMF talks supportive; softer policy rate, import demand and copper-price swings the main risks.
trendAnalysis.projection6m: USD/ZMW 18.00–20.00 range. Direction hinges on fiscal continuity, copper earnings and the pace of further BoZ easing.
